info.title: The Primer API
info.description: The Primer — an AI-generated living storybook and lifelong learning companion for children aged 3-7.

get.description: Returns 200 while the API process is serving requests.

post.description:
Exchange email + password for an access token and a refresh cookie.

`TokenViewBase` already sets `permission_classes = ()` and
`authentication_classes = ()`, which is what a credential endpoint needs;
re-stating them here would only invite someone to "tidy" them into the
project defaults and lock the login page behind a login.
End the session: blacklist the refresh token and delete its cookie.

Rotate the session, using the cookie as the credential.

With `ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS` + `BLACKLIST_AFTER_ROTATION` a *new* refresh
token is issued and the presented one is blacklisted, so the cookie must be
replaced on every call — which `move_to_cookie` does, in the same place it
strips the token from the body.

The token is read from the cookie and **only** from the cookie: accepting a
body as well would leave the old, script-readable path open forever, and a
client that still worked without the cookie is a client that never had to stop
storing the token.

Unauthenticated by inheritance, as in `LoginView` — the refresh token *is* the
credential. `SameSite=Lax` on the cookie is what stops that from being a CSRF
hole; see `apps.accounts.cookies`.

**Its own throttle scope, not `auth`.** This endpoint is called once per page
load, automatically, by every client that has ever been signed in; login is
called by a human, rarely. While they shared one 30/hour budget, a morning of
reloads spent it, `LoginView` then answered 429 to a perfectly correct
password, and — because a failed refresh reads as "your session is over" — the
client had already signed the parent out and sent them to the form that was
refusing them. See `SessionRefreshThrottle`.

get.description:
Narrow a viewset's collection routes to the requesting parent.

`parent_lookup` is the ORM path from the model to the owning parent —
`"parent"` for `Child`, `"child__parent"` for anything hanging off a child.

Detail routes deliberately resolve against the *unscoped* queryset so that
`IsParentOwner` is the thing that rejects them, with a 403. Filtering them
too would give 404 and hide the existence of the row — marginally better
against enumeration, but it would also make an ownership bug indistinguish-
able from a deleted row in the logs, and it is not what the API promises.
Object IDs are UUIDs, so there is nothing here to enumerate.

post.description: Requires an active consent record; returns 403 without one.

Returns the child's in-progress adventure if they have one (**200**), and otherwise generates and persists a story plan and returns the new adventure (**201**). Either way the body carries the SSE URL that streams the beats.

It is idempotent on purpose: a client that has lost the adventure id — a hard refresh, a remount, a second device — must rejoin the same story rather than pay for a new one. A child gets a new adventure once the current one is no longer `in_progress`.

The first beat is generated inside the stream, not here, so the client can open the stream and start the companion's thinking animation immediately.

The stream itself is not in this schema: it is a raw `text/event-stream` endpoint (`GET /api/v1/adventures/{id}/stream`) rather than a DRF view. Its frames are documented in `apps/story/streaming.py`.

get.description:
**200** with the same body as `POST /adventures` when the child has an `in_progress` adventure, **204** when they do not.

This is what the child surface calls on mount: it resumes a story across a reload without the possibility of starting one, so a client bug can cost a request but never a generation.
get.summary: The adventure this child is in the middle of

post.description: Returns immediately with the companion's identity. The reference portrait, canonical expressions and spoken greeting are generated on a worker; poll this endpoint and watch `assets_ready`.

post.description:
Record verifiable parental consent (§13.7).

Create-only on purpose: consent is an audit trail, so a change of mind is a
new record (or a revocation), never an edit of the old one.

get.description: The signed-in parent and their children.

AccessToken.description:
What login and refresh return: the access token, and nothing else.

The refresh half of the pair travels in a cookie the client cannot read, so
this really is the whole body — see `apps.accounts.views`.

AdventureCompanion.description:
The companion, reduced to what the story client needs up front (§18.4).

`voiceId` so the client can pre-warm audio; `name` so the loading scene can
say who is thinking. Nothing else — the portrait and expressions are already
on the companion endpoint.

AdventureStartRequestRequest.description:
The optional client hints on `POST /adventures` (§18.4).

Validated but not yet used: mood- and time-of-day-aware planning is Day 11's
work. Declared now so a client can send it from the start, and so a malformed
`context` is rejected today rather than on the day we begin reading it.

The field is built in `get_fields` rather than declared as a class attribute
because §18.4 names it `context`, and a class attribute by that name shadows
`Serializer.context` — the request/view dictionary every serializer relies on.
The wire name is what the spec fixes; where the field object lives is ours.

* `partial` - Some assets missing

ConsentRecord.description:
Records one verifiable-consent grant.

`parent`, `ip` and `granted_at` are all server-set: a consent record whose
evidence the client could dictate is not evidence.

child_ref.description: Optional child this grant is scoped to. Usually omitted — consent precedes the child.

PaletteColors.description:
The resolved palette.

Declared field by field rather than left as free JSON so the generated
TypeScript client knows a swatch has a `primary` — and so the catalogue keys
arrive in the picker as unions of literals rather than bare strings, which
is what makes an invalid choice a build error instead of a 400.

SignupResponse.description:
Response shape for signup — documented for the generated TS client.

No `refresh` field, deliberately. The refresh token leaves as an `httpOnly`
cookie (`apps.accounts.cookies`); declaring it here would put it back in the
generated client's type and invite someone to store it.
